steps.body: Use the same-size unit for every object. Line up the start, cover the whole length, and count the units.
steps.narration: Use the same-size unit for every object. Line up the start, cover the whole length, and count the units.

widget.prompt: Measure this ribbon of the group with one-unit blocks: align its start and tile it exactly.
widget.successFeedback: Four one-unit blocks tile it exactly — one ribbon measured, in the unit the whole group shares.
widget.alignFeedback: Line up zero with the object's starting end before measuring.
widget.gapOverlapFeedback: The blocks must touch end to end — no spaces and no covering the same part twice.
widget.unitFeedback: Use the same-size unit blocks for every ribbon so the measurements can be compared fairly.

predict.prompt: Half the group is measured in cm, half in paperclips. Comparable?
predict.reveal: A 6 in centimeters and a 6 in paperclips are different lengths wearing the same digit.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents g2g measure group.
invariants: A display and its data are the same information in two forms: every measurement appears exactly once, and counts survive the trip into stacks, rows, and bars for g2g measure group.
misconceptions: Reading a label as a count, dropping repeats while recording, or comparing categories by adding instead of finding the gap.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: What change to the data would the display be FORCED to show — and what change could it silently hide?

explanationVariants: One unit for the whole group.

widget.prompt: What should stay the same when you measure every ribbon?

options.label: The ribbon's color
options.feedback: Color does not change length; use the same-size measuring unit.

options.label: The size of the unit
options.feedback: Correct — the same-size unit makes every length comparable.

options.label: The starting number
options.feedback: A ribbon may start at another mark if you measure the gap correctly.

options.label: The person's name
options.feedback: The measurer's name does not affect the ribbon's length.

hints: Mark to mark is the length.

concept.body: Line up both ribbons at zero and use the same centimeter spaces. Then their lengths can be compared fairly.
concept.narration: Line up both ribbons at zero and use the same centimeter spaces. Then their lengths can be compared fairly.

explanationVariants: One unit for the whole group.

widget.prompt: Which plan makes a fair comparison of two ribbons?

options.label: Use inches for one only
options.feedback: Different units cannot be compared until they are converted.

options.label: Count marks for one only
options.feedback: Measure the spaces for both ribbons, not marks for only one.

options.label: Use centimeters for both
options.feedback: Correct — both ribbons use the same unit.

options.label: Skip the shorter ribbon
options.feedback: Both ribbons must be measured before they can be compared.
